questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My friend is a PHD and was planning on going to Amsterdam. We wanted to live abroad together, why I chose to go to Utrecht and live in Amsterdam with my friend.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Mostly not a problem. I didn't have the possibility of arriving in time for the Welcome week, which complicated things a bit, but overall, not a problem.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not really a lot, mostly showed up for the first classes and took it from there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I chose to live in Amsterdam as I was going with two friends, who studied in Amsterdam. 
Housing market was a bit crazy and we had to pay an illegal fee of 3000€ to the landlord. But we got a nice apartment and were able to claim back the money by threat of legal action.

For anyone looking for apartments in Amsterdam ask !WOON for free advice, they are incredibly helpful.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think I would prefer living on campus if I was going on my own. I basically did not participate in any social life at the university and mostly hung out with my mates in Amsterdam.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Before registering I was given a profile on Osiris, which is the platform where you sign up for courses. For me the process was very simple. They provided information about scheduling of the courses, so you could avoid time table problem. 

Registration was easy, only problem was that the description of the courses was sometimes not thorough.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Course descriptions and a time table planner on UU's website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all my first priorities.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be aware that the difference in teaching methods are very different in bachelor courses and master's courses. 

Master's courses are quite similar to courses I've had in Copenhagen, where the bachelor's courses in Utrecht are filled with almost weekly presentations.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Quite similar to the level at UCPH - bachelor's courses felt a lot like danish high school with participation registration and lecturers not really trusting the students to take responsibility of their own learning. 

Master's level courses were very similar to back home

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I feel like I've described that above

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Natural Language Processing
Responsible Data Science
Advanced Algorithms
Information Security

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them are good in their own ways.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I lived in Amsterdam and did expect to spent quite a lot of money, but did not expect it to be as expensive as it ended up being. 
Apparently, all students in the Netherlands with a Dutch passport have free public transportation, which mean that there are no discount for young people or students.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Trains

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Looked up the possibility of playing football at the university club. But it was ridiculously expensive why I didn't end up doing it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost any sport you can image. There are a lot of different university clubs and so on.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Only thing I really used a lot was participating in Chess tournaments in Amsterdam, cannot really recommend anything in Utrecht as I did not participate in anything.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Doing day bicycle trips to the country side of the Netherlands is amazing. You'll see the country in another way when going through small towns - can recommend a day trip to the island 'Marken'.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Dutch culture is incredibly similar to Danish culture, so wasn't really a problem.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Didn't really do that as I had plenty of friends in Amsterdam

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Bicycle culture, amazing to be able to go anywhere just like in Copenhagen. The architecture and the beauty of Amsterdam was just amazing to experience

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go to the ESN welcome week if you're alone. I met some really nice people with whom I had a lot of fun with.
Be prepared that the dutch students might not be that interested in becoming friends with exchange students so find other exchange students in class.
Go to a lot of cultural events, concerts, theater and so on, both Utrecht and Amsterdam has a lot to offer!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Living abroad made me much more aware on what things make me happy and what things I should prioritize in my at home as well. 
Made me grow a lot as a person to live abroad

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Going to classes not knowing anyone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
